chunks: Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad, from Muḥammad ibn Khālid, from al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd, from Yaḥyā al-Ḥalabī, from ʿImrān ibn Aʿyan, from Juʿayd al-Hamdānī, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him, “By which judgment do you judge?” He said, “The judgment of the family of Dāwūd. So if something is difficult for us, Rūḥ al-Qudus conveys it to us thereby.”

key_terms.آلِ دَاوُدَ: the family of Dāwūd عليه السلام, indicating their mode of judgment
key_terms.أَعْيَانَا: became difficult or burdensome for us
key_terms.تَحْكُمُونَ: you judge or govern in legal decision-making
key_terms.حُكْمٍ: judgment or ruling by which a matter is decided
key_terms.رُوحُ الْقُدُسِ: the Holy Spirit through whom divine communication is conveyed

ai.seo_question: By what judgment do the Imams عليهم السلام judge, and how do they receive knowledge in difficult matters?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the Imam عليه السلام judges by the judgment of the family of Dāwūd and that when a matter becomes difficult, it is conveyed to them by Rūḥ al-Qudus. It highlights the special divine support and authoritative knowledge granted to the Imams عليهم السلام in judgment.
